rows.surface: Syncer verification of commit and record MACs
rows.decision: Two verifiers exist and only the old one is the production path. The old verifier in space_commit.rs checks an ikm and mac inside the commit body, and pds_space_sync.rs hands it the commit from the page body; a host that answers only with the response headers is refused with InvalidSpaceMac or returns a commit the old verifier rejects as malformed, nothing is promoted, and the scheduler logs one line per cycle counting failed targets by a fixed list of reasons, never host text. The new verifier, verify_commit_response in space_mac.rs, reads the Atproto-Space-Commit, Signature-Input and Signature response headers against the one-time key of its own request: exactly one member tagged atproto-space-commit that covers only that header, HMAC-SHA256 over the header re-serialized in the order received compared in constant time, then the five commit fields equal the body's commit and repo and space equal the request's. It is stricter than the pinned package on purpose: a byte sequence in any of the three headers must be the padded base64 of its bytes and no value or parameter may be a decimal, because the package MACs a byte sequence's text as received and writes 1.0 as 1, while the Rust serializer writes the padded bytes and keeps 1.0; such a header is refused as invalid before the MAC, not as a MAC mismatch, so it never triggers the key refresh. It returns a MacVerifiedCommit that only space_mac.rs can make, and the authenticated read in space_host.rs hands back a body only together with one. The synchronizer calls neither, nothing converts between the two verdicts and nothing falls back from one to the other. Still to do: replace the old verifier with the new one in the synchronizer and delete space_commit.rs; op decoding, the set hash and comparing the commit's data with the finished state are not part of the new read. Cross-checked, not run on a real host: every response case of commit-mac.json gets the pinned package's verdict, and the pinned package's response headers for the Rust request verify (stratos-produced.json).

rows.surface: Core space and record URI parser and formatter

A string that starts with at: but not with at:space/, which includes every at:// string, answers invalid-space-marker, and any other string answers invalid-scheme. Both runtime writers use getStratosBacklinks: StratosRecordTransactor behind the sqlite actor store, and PgActorRecordTransactor in the postgres actor store that storage-context.ts builds. rows.decision: The string the feed generator sends, signs and verifies against has one source, boundary_to_space_uri. space_host.rs sends the target space URI as the space query parameter of listRepoOps after validate_request checks only that it is non-empty and at most 2048 bytes; the grammar is checked at the target, in space_sync.rs validate_target. pds_space_sync.rs carries target.space_uri unchanged: it looks the cursor up and stages and discards pages by it, keys the per-target lock on it and passes it to commit verification. space_commit.rs commit_context puts the space URI bytes, length-prefixed, into the context that the commit MAC and signature are checked against, so a commit verifies only when the string is byte for byte the one the commit was made over; a commit made over the earlier spelling fails with a MAC mismatch and is not promoted, and no code retries in another spelling. service_auth.rs mint_space_delegation signs the space URI as the delegation sub claim, and a signed claim is never rewritten. space_mac.rs, the response-header verifier that the synchronizer does not call yet, compares the commit's space and the request's space as bytes after the MAC checks, and a response made for another space is refused as a request mismatch; it parses no URI. rows.surface: Lexicon fields that carry a space record URI
rows.decision: A post's reply.root and reply.parent and a like's or repost's subject are com.atproto.repo.strongRef, and an embedded record is app.bsky.embed.record; their uri fields declare format at-uri. The installed @atproto/syntax 0.7.4 rejects both space spellings as at-uri: the earlier form has more than two path segments, and the current one lacks at://. A record carrying a space record URI therefore passes lexicon validation on boundary writes only through the validation-copy rewrite (see uri-validation-copy-rewrite), and on the legacy write path StratosValidator discards lexicon errors. The vendored com.atproto and app.bsky files are copies and are never edited. The feed generator's getFeed post uri, its viewer like and repost, and getBlob's uri parameter are plain strings whose descriptions state both record forms, so no format check applies to them. The other Stratos fields declared at-uri (repo write outputs, the space getRecord output, hydrateRecord and hydrateRecords, the zone.stratos.defs subject reference) name Stratos-custody records, which keep the repo form. No own field gained or lost a format.
